newsitem.title: USA: U.S. cash crude markets steady on June expiry day.
newsitem.headline: U.S. cash crude markets steady on June expiry day.

text.p: U.S. cash crude prices seemed to find a comfortable trading zone Tuesday afternoon, resting at nearly steady prices ahead of June paper contract expiry.
June West Texas Intermediate/Cushing was steady to four cents lower at $21.50-60 a barrel, compared to July WTI at a steady $20.85-95 mark.
June/July rolls were tracked between minus 34-37 cents.
Traders said domestic grade markets were mostly steady from morning differential levels.
Sweet Louisiana grades were pressured from moving to a premium against benchmark June WTI/Cushing, mainly on expectations for increased levels of Brent for the U.S. Gulf.

Dated Brent was actually bid up after a U.S. refiner bought at July Brent -10 cents, a jump of 10 cents from Monday. The fresh deal was for a June 4-6 loader, and was thought part of a VLCC sailing transatlantic in early June.
Light Louisiana Sweet/St. James was talked at WTI/Cushing minus 5-1 cents, after trading in the morning at even to benchmark.
Midland/WTI rested around last deals at WTI/Cushing -42 cents, with Heavy Louisiana Sweet/Empire pegged at benchmark minus 65-50 cents.
Sour grades failed to move from earlier talk. West Texas Sour/Midland was $1.40 cheaper than WTI/Cushing, with Eugene Island valued at a $1.45 discount.
June Postings Plus was last done at $1.75, and moved between $1.75-1.80.
June Exchange for Physicals (EFPs) were pegged around 15 cents. Crude traders expected to see foreign crude delivered against June NYMEX positions later in the week, aiding EFPs.

EFPs, which allow a buyer or seller to exchange a futures position for physical positions, have gained, as traders work to escape paper positions that might give them a crude other than the benchmark WTI/Cushing once June futures expire.
